newsitem.title: USA: Forwarders already avoiding AA to Latam.
newsitem.headline: Forwarders already avoiding AA to Latam.

text.p: Freight forwarders shipping to Latin America have already begun keeping their freight off American Airlines to avoid any problems in case American's pilots strike, executives told Reuters Thursday.
"As of Monday morning we stopped using American Airlines to avoid any unpleasant surprises," Jose Aguirre, vice president of Miami International Forwarders, said.
The Eagle Companies, another Miami forwarder, also stopped shipping on American on Monday, according to Carlos Murciano, chief operating officer.
American Airline pilots are threatening a strike Saturday at midnight if they do not come to a contract agreement. American was already cancelling international flights beginning Friday.

Unlike passengers, cargo flying out of Miami International Aiport has many alternatives. Experts say there is ample cargo lift out of Miami to Latin America on the 32 scheduled and 18 charter all-cargo carriers that serve MIA.
Although American carries the most cargo through MIA, the other carriers so far have not noticed much difference.
"We have seen a very small amount of new freight," said Ed Lesko, vice president for the Miami-based Arrow Air.
But Aguirre said the other airlines were getting tighter for space and "they are not being as flexible or competitive with rates."
Arrow has had "a number of calls," about booking freight over the next several weeks if American strikes, Lesko said, but many forwarders are taking a wait and see attitude.
"We are ready for whatever comes up," Arrow's senior vice president Jon Batchelor said.
Lesko said: "We could double our capacity to the Caribbean."
Eagle's Murciano said that, if the stike does not take place, American could be flying virtually empty aircraft because passengers made other arrnagements.
"We might see some cheap cargo rates for a while," he said.
